summary: Zev Handel specializes in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and the University of California, Berkeley (1992, 1998). Around 1999, he became a Professor at the University of Washington.
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied under Sen Wang and served as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested in 2014).

Zhaohua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (attested 2018), and he taught Kevin Buckelew.

Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and was an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. Liu completed an MA at the University of Munich by 2005 and an MA at Lanzhou University by 2009.
Zhengyan Fan works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fan is a PhD researcher and held a post at Ghent University in 2026.
Zhenhua (1922–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yinshun in 1952. In 1992, he is attested as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute.

Zhihua Yao works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002), was a professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005), and joined The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005).
Zhiqing Wang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Wang studied at Lanzhou University from 2006 to 2009 and at East China Normal University in 2021.

Zhiru Ng works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Ng completed an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan (-1993) and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. She held posts at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and Fo Guang University (2026).

Zhiyi Yang specializes in sinology. She studied at Peking University, Princeton University under Martin Kern (PhD 2012), and Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and became a Professor at Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015, post 2025).

Zhonghui Cui works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, later serving as an academic consultant there (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) worked in history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied under Su Bai from around 1952 to 1956 and served as director at the Palace Museum from around 1987 to 1991.

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965), where he worked (~1965–1978), before serving at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002) and Soka University (~1999–2000).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li specializes in Buddhist studies. Li studied at Komazawa University and served as a DC special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, both attested in 2015.

Zolboo Sandagjav specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Sandagjav studied at the National University of Mongolia, Delhi, Lausanne, and Bern, later serving as an assistant lecturer at the University of Bern from 2024 to 2025.
Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium until 1895 and at Eötvös Loránd University from 1895 to 1900.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ganden Shartse and Gyuto monasteries under Dechen Nyingpo and Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937–1946) and director/Rektor of CIHTS (1965, 1967–1971).
